correctness.rationale: Full proof checks fixed-degree sampling normalization and the cyclic-set enumerator; exact transfer tail differences follow by factoring (1+az)(1+bz). The strict Newton ratio establishes the single-crossing cyclic mass law and exact TV; a total-positive Stirling kernel extends one crossing to components; a unit-subset injection gives the sharp envelope and explicit maximizing index. The constructed standalone exact rational verifier passed 91,476 assertions including 873,611 fully enumerated mappings through n=7 and integer degree partition transfers through n=11. Finite checks do not replace the all-size arguments.

originality.rationale: The 2006/2008 exact cyclic-vertex distribution and cycle-count Stirling transform are prior and not claimed new. The assessed joint contribution is the exact deterministic balancing-transfer response, unique one-crossing, sharp total-variation identity/profile envelope, the TP2 component-count lift, and explicit failure of stronger likelihood-ratio ordering. Comparisons by mathematical implication did not identify a directly dominating theorem in the full inspected 2006/2008 primary paper, or in scoped literature and published-result searches. Classical symmetric-function and TP2 ingredients could potentially hide an older equivalent formulation; priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: The single-crossing conclusion may appear implicitly in historic symmetric-function/majorization comparisons that were not discoverable in targeted searches.
Some older general total-positivity and symmetric-function sources may supply an implicit strengthening; the review is not exhaustive.
No independent scientific audit or human priority assessment has been performed.

value.rationale: The result quantifies exactly how balancing two prescribed in-degrees changes the entire cyclic-vertex law, rather than just a mean or asymptotic scale. The sharp TV identity and extremal integer residual-degree profile are natural stability information for a degree-conditioned random functional digraph. Single crossing of the component count and a concrete minimal likelihood-ratio obstruction make the distribution-order boundary mathematically substantive.
